structure.title: The governing distinction
structure.text: The opening separates what depends on our choices from what does not. Later advice keeps applying this distinction to daily disturbances.

structure.title: Practice in company
structure.text: Short sections examine possessions, loss, conversation, roles, and philosophical training. The arrangement invites repeated use rather than a single unfolding demonstration.

people.name: Epictetus
people.text: A former slave who became a famous Stoic teacher, whose sayings were collected by his student Arrian into this short handbook.

people.name: Assent
people.text: The choice to agree that an impression is true, which Epictetus says is always in our power, and where all our freedom and our troubles begin.

people.name: Role
people.text: The part one plays as a son, a parent, a citizen, or a friend, which Epictetus says tells you what you owe to others, whatever they do.

context.title: What depends on us
context.text: The distinction concerns judgment and choice, not a promise that sufficient willpower can control events or other people.
context.takeaway: Agency does not imply control of outcomes.

passages.quote: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.

context.title: A handbook
context.text: These compressed instructions assume a larger practice of philosophical learning. Their brevity can conceal the effort needed to apply them.
context.takeaway: A maxim is an exercise, not a cure.

notice.why: The text locates freedom in examining an impression.
Detachment from approval does not eliminate duties.

opening: Someone insults you, a plan falls apart, a person whose approval you wanted looks elsewhere. Epictetus treats these ordinary injuries as evidence of a dangerous arrangement: your peace depends on things other people can withhold. A former slave, he proposes a discipline severe enough to survive that discovery. His instructions keep returning responsibility to judgments and choices, even when circumstances are brutal. The difficulty begins where the advice gets specific, asking what you are prepared to stop demanding from the world.
